one_liner: LD_PRELOAD shim that reroutes FFTW3 1-D power-of-two complex float FFTs to the original Raspberry Pi's VideoCore IV GPU.
what_it_does: Builds libgpufftwf.so and libgpufftw.so, which intercept fftwf_plan_dft_1d / fftwf_execute / fftwf_destroy_plan (and the double-precision versions) through LD_PRELOAD and dlsym(RTLD_NEXT), so an unmodified FFTW3 binary runs its 1-D complex transforms on the GPU. A launcher (sudo ./gpu_fftw [-d] -- program args) sets LD_PRELOAD and execs the program; anything it cannot handle (non-power-of-two N, N < 256, GPU setup failure, GPU_FFTW_DISABLE set) falls back to the real FFTW plan. A minimal Fortran execute hook is included for GNU Fortran.
how_it_is_fast: The work is done by Andrew Holme's GPU_FFT 2.0 (bundled as hello_fft/): per-size hand-written QPU shader binaries that compute the transform in 2 to 4 passes of radix-16/32/64 butterflies (N=1,024 is two radix-32 passes) spread over the 8 VideoCore IV QPUs, with twiddles and ping-pong buffers in GPU-shared memory. For small batches (N*jobs <= 20480) it launches the shaders by poking V3D registers directly through /dev/mem and busy-waits; larger jobs go through the firmware mailbox. The speedup is simply that the Pi 1's ARM11 CPU running FFTW is much slower than the QPUs.
when_to_use: Legacy Raspberry Pi 1 / Zero-class (BCM2835, ARMv6) systems running an existing FFTW3-linked program you cannot recompile, e.g. SDR or audio spectrum tools.
1-D complex single-precision FFTs of power-of-two length 2^8 to 2^21 where the plan is reused and the program fills the input before planning.
Quick experiments to see whether GPU offload helps an FFT-bound Pi 1 workload before porting code to the GPU_FFT API directly.
when_not_to_use: Any program that plans once and then writes new data into the input array before each fftw_execute: the shim copies the input to GPU memory only at plan time, so later executes transform the stale plan-time data.

Raspberry Pi 2/3/4/5 or any non-Pi hardware: the bundled GPU_FFT 2.0 hard-codes the BCM2835 peripheral base 0x20000000, and open issue #1 reports the self-test override check failing on a Pi 3 (GPU/FFTW difference 0 ppm, i.e. the GPU path apparently never ran).
Double precision work: the -d 'double squashing' mode silently computes double requests in float.
2-D/3-D, real-to-complex, batched (plan_many), new-array execute (fftw_execute_dft) or threaded FFTW use: none are intercepted.
Production or multi-user systems: requires root (/dev/mem mapping, mknod of /dev/gpu_mb), runs the target program as root with LD_PRELOAD, and the README calls it an early alpha.

integration.dependencies: FFTW3 (libfftw3 and libfftw3f, called via dlsym RTLD_NEXT), libdl, bundled GPU_FFT 2.0 (hello_fft, BSD-3-Clause), root access to /dev/mem and the VideoCore mailbox
integration.platforms: Raspberry Pi with BCM2835 / VideoCore IV (Pi 1, Zero); Linux only
integration.thread_safety: Not thread-safe: plans live in a static 1024-slot array with an unlocked counter, the mailbox handle is a static, and the shim calls setenv/unsetenv on every plan to signal GPU use.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — binary drop-in via LD_PRELOAD for fftw(f)_plan_dft_1d + execute + destroy_plan only; every 1-D DFT plan (even a fallback one) becomes a wrapper struct, so passing it to any other FFTW function (fftw_execute_dft, fftw_print_plan, fftw_flops) hands FFTW a foreign pointer

gotchas: Plan slots are taken as mplan_arr[mplan_n++] and freed by decrementing mplan_n, so destroying plans out of LIFO order lets the next plan overwrite a live one; past 1024 live plans the fallback path dereferences a NULL metaplan.
The input array is copied to GPU memory inside fftw_plan_dft_1d and never again; FFTW_MEASURE-style 'plan first, fill later' code gets wrong results with no error.

Planner flags (FFTW_MEASURE, FFTW_PATIENT, wisdom) are ignored on the GPU path; each GPU plan allocates and maps its own VideoCore memory, so many concurrent plans can exhaust GPU memory (then it falls back to FFTW).
The launcher passes child arguments poorly (open issue #2: the child's flags are parsed as gpu_fftw options unless separated with --).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No catalogued sibling targets the Raspberry Pi GPU; on a Pi 1/Zero with an unmodifiable FFTW binary this is the only drop-in, while for new code or newer Pis a NEON CPU library such as Ne10, or PFFFT/muFFT, is the safer choice.
verified_claims_summary: The project's own self-test, on an unnamed Raspberry Pi (Makefile targets ARMv6, so Pi 1 class), timed 1,000 forward 1,024-point complex float FFTs: 11,523 FFT/s on the GPU versus 1,619 FFT/s for CPU fftw3f with an FFTW_ESTIMATE plan (7.1x); plan creation and the GPU path's one-time input copy are outside the timed loop, and the compiler/FFTW versions are not stated.
status_note: Abandoned since January 2015 (two open, unanswered issues) and alpha quality; MIT-licensed and small, but only of historical or Pi-1-specific interest given its stale-input and plan-slot bugs.
